title: Compression of Emotion in Language Model Representations
summary: Across seven language models on GoEmotions, K-means clustering of emotion-prompted hidden representations most clearly separated positive from negative emotion rather than all 28 labels, while linear probes retained fine-grained predictive information. This characterizes the tested representations and protocol, not all model behavior.
ai_technology: Unsupervised representation geometry and emotion classification probes

evidence.tested: Across seven language models on GoEmotions, K-means clustering of emotion-prompted hidden representations most clearly separated positive from negative emotion rather than all 28 labels, while linear probes retained fine-grained predictive information. This characterizes the tested representations and protocol, not all model behavior.
evidence.unknown: The study evaluates the reported models and datasets only; broader generalization and real-world deployment outcomes were not established.
evidence.ai_role: The authors clustered emotion-prompted final-token hidden representations with K-means and compared the resulting geometry with fine-grained labels and linear-probe performance.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
